title: Garden and Thorn
premise: In the city of Vharrow, where magic was outlawed after the Sundering, Dominic Delacroix sells harmless charms to survive while the last guild of true mages fades into memory. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into his hands, Dominic discovers the route to the Thornwood, where an ancient entity called the Verdant has bound itself to the king's crown and is slowly consuming the realm through an endless winter. Pursued by the king's witch-hunters and shadowed by Sera, a huntress sworn to the crown who becomes his reluctant ally and something more, Dominic must reach the Thornwood and unbind the king before the long winter falls forever. In the end, Dominic severs the Verdant at the cost of his own latent magic, freeing the king but leaving the guild's legacy in his hands alone — and he and Sera choose love and a rebuilt guild over the safety of old laws.
about_author: Beatrix Delacroix is the pen name of a former botanist who left research to write fantasy steeped in folklore of hedge-witches and winter courts. She lives in a drafty farmhouse where she keeps an unruly garden that, she insists, is only metaphorically enchanted.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Winter
chapters.summary: Dominic Delacroix hawks protective charms in Vharrow's frost-choked markets, hiding his guild training from the Wardens who burn mages. His grandmother's guild medallion is all that remains of a dying order. When a Warden raid nearly exposes him, Dominic realizes the city is growing more dangerous by the season — and the winter is growing longer. POV: Dominic. Beat: weary survival, quiet dread.

chapters.title: The Dying Courier
chapters.summary: A bloodied stranger collapses in Dominic's shop, pressing a wax-sealed map into his hands and whispering 'the Thornwood remembers' before dying. Dominic finds the map marked with the guild's lost sigil — a route only a Delacroix could read. Wardens arrive moments later, forcing him to flee with nothing but the map and his medallion. POV: Dominic. Beat: shock, reluctant destiny.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wears
chapters.summary: In the palace, Sera Vane, huntress of the royal order, reports the courier's death to her commander. She glimpses the king at council — and sees something move beneath his skin, a green flicker behind his eyes that no one else acknowledges. Her sworn loyalty wars with what she witnessed. POV: Sera. Beat: unease, first crack in duty.

chapters.title: Road Out of Vharrow
chapters.summary: Dominic escapes the city through the sewers with help of an old guild contact, Maren, who warns him the map leads to the Verdant — the entity the guild once bound to protect the realm, and which now wears the king. On the frozen north road, Dominic uses small magic for the first time in years and feels the guild's power stir. POV: Dominic. Beat: fear giving way to exhilaration.

chapters.title: The Huntress's Trail
chapters.summary: Sera is ordered to hunt the courier's killer — Dominic. Tracking him through the pinewastes, she expects a murderer and finds instead a terrified charm-seller who saves her from a frost-wraith with hedge-magic that should be impossible. She takes him prisoner rather than kill him, telling herself it's procedure. POV: Sera. Beat: conflict between oath and instinct.

chapters.title: Prisoner of the Snow Road
chapters.summary: Bound and marching toward the capital, Dominic talks — about the Verdant, the guild's history, the green thing behind the king's eyes. Sera refuses to believe him until nightfall, when the prisoner and captor are attacked by Warden-hounds that should only obey the crown. Someone wants them both dead. POV: Sera. Beat: reluctant alliance, shared danger.

chapters.title: The Hollow Village
chapters.summary: They shelter in a village where every hearth is cold and the people move like sleepwalkers, tending gardens that bloom impossibly in deep winter. Dominic recognizes the Verdant's touch — it's spreading, feeding on the land ahead of the king's decline. Sera watches him heal a child and can no longer call his magic a crime. POV: Dominic. Beat: horror and tenderness intertwined.

chapters.title: Orders from the Green King
chapters.summary: In Vharrow, the king — or the thing wearing him — dispatches the Warden-Captain Corvane to retrieve the map and silence all who've seen it. We learn the Verdant's bargain: eternal spring promised, endless winter delivered. The court withers as the crown's hunger grows. POV: Corvane. Beat: menace, the scale of the threat revealed.

chapters.title: Maren's Price
chapters.summary: Dominic and Sera reach Maren's safehouse, where Dominic learns the unbinding requires a Delacroix's blood and the guild's three lost relics — and that his grandmother died trying to gather them. Maren gives him the first, a seed-charm, at a price: he must rebuild the guild afterward. Sera chooses to stay with him, deserting her order. POV: Dominic. Beat: inheritance of burden, Sera's choice.

chapters.title: Corvane's Web
chapters.summary: Corvane's agents close in; Maren is captured covering their escape, and Dominic must choose between rescuing her and keeping the map safe. He chooses the map, hating himself. Sera, who once served the law that now serves the Verdant, tells him mercy can wait until the realm is saved. POV: Sera. Beat: guilt, the cost of the larger fight.

chapters.title: The Relic in the Deep
chapters.summary: Beneath a frozen abbey, the second relic — the guild's chalice — lies in a warded crypt. Dominic's blood opens the seal, and visions of the guild's founders show him the truth of the original binding: the Verdant was never evil, only starving, betrayed by the bargain it was forced to accept. POV: Dominic. Beat: revelation, sympathy for the monster.

chapters.title: What Sera Buried
chapters.summary: By the fire, Sera confesses: years ago she reported her own brother, a hedge-mage, to the Wardens. He burned. Her loyalty to the crown was penance, and now the crown itself is the corruption. Dominic tells her the guild forgave worse. Something unspoken between them finally takes shape. POV: Sera. Beat: confession, love kindling against duty's ruins.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Pass
chapters.summary: Corvane ambushes them at Thorn Pass with Warden-hounds and frost-wraiths. Sera fights like someone settling old debts; Dominic, pushed to his limits, unleashes guild-magic he barely controls. They win the pass but Dominic is wounded, and the wound festers with the Verdant's green touch. POV: Dominic. Beat: costly victory, ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Third Relic's Keeper
chapters.summary: The final relic — the guild's blade — is held by a hermit who was once the guild's last master: Dominic's grandmother, alive, exiled, and bitter. She refuses to hand it over, believing the Verdant cannot be unbound without killing the king. She tests Dominic with the blade's judgment. POV: Dominic. Beat: family reckoning, hard truths.

chapters.title: The Test of the Blade
chapters.summary: The blade shows Dominic two futures: unbinding the Verdant saves the king but dooms the land to slow natural decay, while letting the Verdant reign promises false spring and true enslavement. Dominic chooses the harder mercy — unbinding, and rebuilding what comes after. His grandmother yields the blade and her blessing. POV: Dominic. Beat: moral clarity earned, not given.

chapters.title: The Green Court
chapters.summary: Sera infiltrates the palace as a returning huntress, discovering the court half-consumed — courtiers with vines beneath their skin, the queen already gone. She reaches the king's chamber and sees the Verdant fully: a vast green consciousness wearing a dying man. It speaks to her, offering her brother back. POV: Sera. Beat: temptation at the heart of power.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Corvane, fully corrupted, seizes the capital and declares the Long Winter — the Verdant's final feeding. Maren escapes her cell and sends warning. Dominic and his grandmother race toward Vharrow as the land itself begins to die, frost devouring the Thornwood's edge. POV: Corvane. Beat: the darkest hour, everything staked.

chapters.title: Storming the Pale Palace
chapters.summary: Dominic, Sera, and the grandmother breach the palace through the old guild tunnels. Sera confronts Corvane while Dominic and his grandmother reach the throne room, where the king begs through the Verdant's grip for release. The grandmother begins the unbinding rite; Corvane's forces break through. POV: Sera. Beat: desperate courage, all threads converging.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: The rite demands a Delacroix's blood and magic entire. The grandmother falls to Corvane's blade; Dominic completes the unbinding, pouring his guild-gift into severing the Verdant from the king. The Verdant, freed and fading, thanks him and returns the stolen spring. Dominic's magic dies with the binding. The king wakes, mortal and weeping. POV: Dominic. Beat: sacrifice, climax, grief and release.

chapters.title: After the Frost
chapters.summary: The Long Winter breaks. Corvane, freed from the Verdant's grip, surrenders and faces judgment; Sera testifies to what the crown became. The king, ashamed, lifts the ban on magic and asks the guild's forgiveness. Dominic, magicless, holds the medallion and wonders what he is now — and what the guild can become. POV: Sera. Beat: aftermath, justice, uncertain hope.

chapters.title: Seeds in Ashen Ground
chapters.summary: Dominic and Sera rebuild the guild not as a secret order but as a school, teaching hedge-craft openly in the Thornwood's recovering shade. Maren joins them; the first students arrive. Dominic cannot cast, but he can teach — and the land remembers the guild that freed it. POV: Dominic. Beat: renewal, purpose found in loss.

chapters.title: Garden and Thorn
chapters.summary: One year on, in the guild's new garden, Dominic and Sera plant a tree over his grandmother's grave. The Verdant's last gift — a single green shoot that never frosts — blooms beside it. Love, law, and magic find their new balance. The thorn remains, but so does the garden. POV: Dominic. Beat: resolution, quiet joy, earned peace.
